bug_semantics: An attacker can place OSC/CSI control bytes in a filesystem entry name. When a user scans that entry in `dua i`, marks it, and quits without deleting it, the marked `PathBuf` is taken from the TUI mark pane. After `drop(terminal)` has restored the real terminal, the program passed `path.display()` directly to `println!`. No encoding or control-character filtering occurred at that output boundary, so a terminal emulator interpreted the embedded bytes rather than displaying an inert path, enabling such effects as terminal-title spoofing or clipboard manipulation.
flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 017cbd7b4c3e57e1a98fbc595159be39bc97c708 implemented the marked-path-on-exit feature end to end: it added `MarkPane::into_paths`, extracted the remaining marked filesystem paths from the application, and added `println!("{}", path.display())` after the terminal object was dropped. That commit first created both the attacker-controlled path flow and the unsanitized post-TUI terminal sink; its immediate parent contains neither the extraction helper nor this print loop.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object identifies both author and committer as `Sebastian Thiel <sebastian.thiel@icloud.com>` and its complete message is `Print marked items upon exit if these are left in the marked pane` followed only by `Fixes #87`; there is no bot identity, `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, model name, or other AI trailer/marker on the BIC.
evidence: Vulnerability and attack path: the first-party report https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/365 identifies `src/main.rs` after terminal teardown, traces `paths` to `app.window.mark.take().map(|pane| pane.into_paths())`, and states that a marked crafted filename reaches `println!` unchanged; it confirms the vulnerable tip b6e7cafd305c150834eb887e1de99bcdd3fca85d and released version 2.41.1. The frozen GHSA-2m2p-wc26-4j7x/CVE-2026-73479 bundle describes the same OSC/CSI injection and references b6e7cafd305c150834eb887e1de99bcdd3fca85d as affected history, not as the repair. Origin trace: `git log -L '/if let Some(paths) = paths {/',+6:src/main.rs a2d375d7fdb4eecc287ad87715a3f021951e3e6d^` traces the vulnerable print back to 017cbd7b4c3e57e1a98fbc595159be39bc97c708; the only later edits in that line history before the fix are the 2024 control-flow cleanup 13c381bebc6a64e553ec11793ec8880f868e712c and the 2026 semicolon-only change 9e36f030b882258e70fa4daf5591146d934f72eb. `git show --format=raw 017cbd...` proves it is a one-parent commit with parent c8d5650be77e000801b282c4c0a3861e710de6d8 and shows the causal additions at `src/interactive/widgets/mark.rs:105`, `src/main.rs:99`, and `src/main.rs:117` in the BIC tree. Direct parent-tree verification: `git grep -n -E 'into_paths|println!\("\{\}", path\.display\(\)\)' c8d5650... -- src/main.rs src/interactive/widgets/mark.rs` returns no match, while the identical command on 017cbd... returns `into_paths` at mark.rs:105, its call at main.rs:99, and the raw print at main.rs:117. The BIC source shows `drop(terminal)` and stdout flush before that print. Feature intent is independently recorded by https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/87, which asked to print marked paths and whose maintainer stated that v2.13 would print them on quit. Version boundary: c8d5650be77e000801b282c4c0a3861e710de6d8 is exactly tag v2.12.2; `merge-base --is-ancestor` shows the BIC absent from v2.12.2 and present in v2.13.0. `git tag --contains 017cbd...` begins at v2.13.0 and includes every dua-cli tag through v2.41.1. The direct fix is absent from v2.41.1 and is an ancestor of v2.42.0; v2.42.0's signed tag/release notes explicitly list `sanitize control characters in marked path output`. Fix: https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/pull/366 and a2d375d7fdb4eecc287ad87715a3f021951e3e6d replace direct display with control-character filtering. Review commit 8521d0d0231a6e95b7b9cc350b2eb2fc570a2833 narrows filtering to terminal stdout so redirected machine-readable paths stay raw. Landing merge f515d36174efeba2cdc2148fbb684f201df9ddad has parents b6e7cafd305c150834eb887e1de99bcdd3fca85d and 8521d0d0231a6e95b7b9cc350b2eb2fc570a2833; `git diff f515d...^1 f515d... -- src/main.rs` shows the final `marked_path_for_output` helper, `stdout.is_terminal()` gate, sanitized print, and regression test. `git grep` on the merge tree finds the helper and sanitized call at src/main.rs:64 and :194 and no raw `println!("{}", path.display())`. Ancestry checks prove 017cbd... -> a2d375... -> f515d.... BIC-only AI evidence: `git show -s --format='author=%an <%ae>%ncommitter=%cn <%ce>%n%B' 017cbd...` returns the same human author/committer and only the two-line subject/`Fixes #87` message quoted in `ai_marker`.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior was not inherited from the TUI renderer: ratatui protected in-TUI display, while the security boundary was crossed only after terminal teardown. The smallest causal change is therefore the 2021 feature commit that first exported marked filesystem paths and printed them directly to the restored terminal. Line history rules out later moves and cleanups as origin, and the candidate-vs-immediate-parent tree comparison proves the entire vulnerable data flow and sink were absent in c8d5650.... No squash decomposition is applicable because 017cbd... is an atomic, non-merge, one-parent commit whose diff itself adds the mechanism. Release ancestry brackets introduction between v2.12.2 and v2.13.0 and repair between vulnerable v2.41.1 and fixed v2.42.0. The 2026 direct fix and its review refinement close exactly the post-TUI terminal-output flaw, and the merge commit is the repository landing point. Finally, attribution is intentionally restricted to the BIC commit object: it contains only Sebastian Thiel's human author/committer identities and no AI authorship marker. Any AI activity around the 2026 review/fix is later and cannot attribute the 2021 BIC. With a real BIC, verified parent absence, closed version/fix lifecycle, and absent BIC commit-object AI signal, the supported verdict is NOT_AI.
